why: This checker guards a downgrade that nothing else refuses. kagent admits a ModelConfig with a spec.tls block beside an http:// baseUrl: nothing fails, the block is inert, the seam is plaintext, and the manifest reads as configured. It also admits an https:// baseUrl with no tls block, which fails every call as a generic connection error far from its cause. So the checker has to fail in every way it could stop noticing either half — the scheme test, the missing-authority test, the disableVerify test, the two identity tests, the recogniser that finds no seam URLs or every URL, the FLOOR that stops a scan which read nothing from printing the clean verdict, the enumeration that decides which files are read at all, and a verdict computed and dropped. The FIXTURES are mutated too: a self-test whose broken cases stop being broken passes while checking nothing, and that is the failure this harness cannot otherwise see.

mutations.name: a plaintext seam URL is no longer a problem
mutations.breaks: The half that matters most. Every manifest could point at the seam over http, carry a tls block that is never used, and read exactly like one that is verified.

mutations.name: an https seam with no authority passes
mutations.breaks: The other half. The agent verifies against the system trust store, which has never heard of the plane, and every call fails with a message that names nothing.

mutations.name: verification may be disabled
mutations.breaks: The rule that a seam nobody verifies is weaker than a plaintext one that never claimed to be verified — it costs the same certificate machinery and buys nothing.

mutations.name: any authority is accepted, not only the plane's
mutations.breaks: The identity of the trust anchor. A manifest naming a Secret that does not exist reads clean here and is refused by kagent later, as a broken seam rather than a typo.

mutations.name: any key inside the authority Secret is accepted
mutations.breaks: The other half of the same identity. kagent refuses a caCertSecretKey the Secret does not carry, and reports it on the resource's own condition where nobody is looking.

mutations.name: no URL is recognised as a seam
mutations.breaks: The recogniser, from the empty side: every manifest is treated as pointing somewhere else, so the whole file passes while examining nothing. Enumerated and examined are separate checks.

mutations.name: every URL is recognised as a seam
mutations.breaks: The recogniser from the other side. An ungoverned ModelConfig pointing at Ollama is required to name the plane's authority — a check that fails on documents it has no business reading is a check people turn off.

mutations.name: nested URLs stop being found
mutations.breaks: The walk. A ModelConfig's baseUrl is nested under its provider block, so a reader that only looks at the top level finds no seam URLs at all and reports every manifest clean.

mutations.name: the self-test's broken fixtures stop being broken
mutations.breaks: The FIXTURE, which no other mutation touches. The plaintext case becomes a correct manifest and its expectation goes unmet. One case, not all of them — but the point stands: a self-test whose broken inputs stop being broken is exactly as green as one that checks everything.

mutations.name: a correct manifest is rejected
mutations.breaks: The other direction, and the one a breakage-only self-test cannot see: a checker that rejects everything catches every mutation above and is useless. The clean manifest is what says so.

mutations.breaks: The same over-reach reached through the trust anchor: an ungoverned ModelConfig pointing at a real provider is told to name the plane's authority, and a check that fails on documents it has no business reading is a check people turn off.
